question: What will be the ending value of the ICE BofA US High Yield Option-Adjusted Spread for these biweekly periods of Q4 2026? (Nov 23 - Dec 4)

calls.reasoning: FRED last print 3.52 (Nov 19), after widening from 3.23 on Nov 13. On Nov 20 the S&P fell 3.7% into a correction (VIX 35.9), with an Nvidia SEC probe and AI-credit/CCC stress. HYG NAV fell 0.39% despite a ~12bp Treasury rally, implying ~+20-28bp, so Nov 20 is likely ~3.70-3.78. Reference class: 10-day spread moves after VIX>30 spikes; these often mean-revert (Aug 2024, Apr 2025, Mar 2026), but a Fed hike priced for Dec 9, 10y near 5% and a developing AI credit unwind give fat right-tail risk (Dec 2018 analog). Unconditional median ~3.68, 10-90 ~3.30-4.25, so ~43.5% mass above 3.745 declared as an upper escape; percentiles are conditional on landing in range. No Polymarket/Kalshi/Manifold market found.

calls.reasoning: FRED's last print is 3.52 (Nov 19). On Fri Nov 20 the S&P 500 fell 3.7% and the VIX closed at 35.89. Bloomberg's HY spread widened 23bp to 367 (+51bp on the week); with ICE running ~7-8bp above Bloomberg, ICE on Nov 20 is likely ~3.72-3.78, right at the 3.745 upper bound. Reference class: recent spikes in this series (Aug 2024, Apr 2025, Oct 2025, Mar 2026) gave back 50-100% of the spike within two weeks, and December seasonality favors tightening, so the median drifts to ~3.6. Against that: a two-month persistent trend, a hawkish Fed, CCC distress, the ongoing AI unwind, PCE on Nov 25 and thin holiday liquidity keep continuation risk high. I put ~32% on the Dec 4 value being above 3.745. Percentiles describe the distribution conditional on landing in range. No prediction market found.
